exercises.name: Straight Arm Lat Pulldown (Cable)

source_english.description: A straight-arm cable pulldown pulls a high cable bar to the thighs with nearly straight elbows.
instructions: Attach a straight bar to the high pulley and stand facing the machine.
Grip the bar overhand with arms extended and elbows softly unlocked.
Pull the bar down in an arc to the thighs while keeping the elbows nearly fixed.
Pause, then return the bar overhead under control.
form_cues: Pull the bar to the thighs with the lats.
Keep the ribs stacked over the pelvis.
source_english.safety_note: Use a cable load that allows a smooth shoulder arc without forcing overhead range.

exercises.name: Reverse Grip Lat Pulldown (Cable)

source_english.description: Reverse Grip Lat Pulldown (Cable) pulls the band, cable bar, or machine handles from overhead toward the upper chest while the torso stays braced.
instructions: Adjust the cable machine so that the pulldown bar is at a height above your head.
Sit down on the seat and grab the pulldown bar with an underhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and lean back slightly.
Pull the bar down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly release the bar back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the ribs stacked and shoulders down.
Drive the elbows toward the torso.
Control the return to the start.
common_mistakes: Leaning or swinging to move the load.
source_english.safety_note: Use a secure station and a load or assistance level you can control through the full range.
